stem: Sibling plants from the same cross differ sharply in aroma and architecture. Which explanation best fits a segregating population?
choices: Recombination and segregation can produce different allele combinations among siblings
All siblings from one cross must be genetically identical
The differences prove the seed labels were wrong
Environment can never contribute to sibling differences
rationale: Segregation and recombination generate different allele combinations among sexually produced siblings, while environment can further affect observed phenotype.
